Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. Author-created scientific text and derived materials are released under CC BY 4.0 where applicable; original author-created software is released under the MIT License unless stated otherwise.

items.summary: This paper develops a preliminary account of normative formation under conditions in which heterogeneous sources possess unequal capacities to generate, stabilize, interpret, circulate, and revise normative structures. Normative formation is used broadly for the emergence of relatively stable concepts, evaluative distinctions, interpretive conventions, practical expectations, and recognized modes of reasoning and action; normative grammar serves only as an analytical analogy for partially stabilized relations among them. The central concern is relational and temporal. Differences in generative capacity may affect the relative influence of normative sources and, under some conditions, the later conditions through which other sources can participate in formation. The paper therefore distinguishes generative capacity from realized normative influence and develops the provisional concepts of endogenous weighting, generative crowding-out, and normative closure. Three case studies refine the framework from different directions: philosophical claim formation foregrounds argumentative provenance; international law foregrounds practice, identification, interpretation, and legally relevant history; aesthetic norm formation foregrounds pre-explicit differentiation and the possible co-formation of judgment and norm. The later analysis develops a trajectory-sensitive perspective in which the significance of asymmetry depends partly on its provenance, persistence, revisability, self-reinforcement, and effects on future generative capacities. The discussion remains exploratory and offers neither a complete theory of normativity or power nor a general metric of justice or institutional design.
items.title: A Preliminary Discussion of Normative Formation under Asymmetric Generative Capacity

items.summary: This package contains the data and the code that reproduce every table, figure and number reported in the article. A single script ( run_all.sh ) runs all steps in about 25 seconds and ends by checking that each generated output is byte-for-byte identical to the one used in the manuscript. What the paper does. Spanish households increasingly buy their food with the preparation already done. The paper measures this with an ordinal index of Domestic Labour Substitution (DLS) built on eleven "ladders" — market forms of the same food, ordered by the amount of household preparation they displace to the market — and asks whether the shift reflects the rising value of household time or the falling relative price of processed food. A conditional-logit model of the choice among forms implies that a price change common to all households cancels, to first order, in the gap between household groups shopping in the same market, which directs the test to the COVID-19 lockdown as a shock to the relative value of time. Contents. data/raw/mapa/ — the 14 annual files of the Spanish household food consumption panel ( Panel de Consumo Alimentario en los Hogares , MAPA), 2014–2025, unaltered, with a manifest listing the source URL, size and SHA-256 checksum of each file. data/raw/eurostat/ — snapshots of the Eurostat series used: regional employment rates ( lfst_r_lfe2emprt ), national employment and participation rates ( lfsi_emp_a ) and time use by labour status ( tus_00selfstat ), each with its query URLs. code/ — numbered scripts: extraction of the ladders, recovery of the population behind each published household segment, time-use figures, all estimates and tests, the figure, and a final byte-for-byte check against the reference outputs. Optional scripts re-download the source data and verify the checksums. reference/ — the tables and numbers as published in the article. README.md — data provenance and licensing, computational requirements, description of each program, and the mapping from each table, figure and in-text number to the script that produces it, following the Social Science Data Editors template. Requirements. Python 3.11 with numpy, openpyxl and matplotlib ( requirements.txt ). The random seed is fixed, so the wild cluster bootstrap p-values reproduce exactly. Data sources and terms. MAPA data are reproduced unaltered under the reuse terms of the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (the source must be cited and the update metadata preserved; Ley 37/2007). Eurostat data are reused under CC BY 4.0 (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU). The code is released under the MIT License (see LICENSE ). Related article. Recio-Román, A., Recio-Menéndez, M., & Román-González, M. V. (2026). Who Cooks When the Supermarket Cooks? The Value of Time and the Market Substitution of Domestic Food Preparation in Spain. items.summary: A contiguous cartogram is a map whose area is proportional to a quantity such as population. The defining condition, that the Jacobian determinant of the deformation equals the density, is one equation for two unknown functions, so every cartogram method adds a tie-breaker, usually implicitly. Optimal transport makes the tie-breaker explicit: among all density-equalising maps of the frame onto itself, take the one that moves the population least in the mean-square sense. By Brenier's theorem that map is the gradient of a convex potential, so it has no local rotation anywhere and cannot fold. We compute this map for the world population of 2025 on a 4096 by 4096 Mercator grid (10 km cells) from the GHS-POP raster, using the fixed-point Monge-Ampère iteration of Benamou, Froese and Oberman with spectral Poisson solves, continuation in the population share and an ocean-only buffer, on a laptop GPU. Against a Gastner-Newman diffusion cartogram of the same density we find the same transport cost to within 0.4 per cent and density errors of a few per cent for both, but a median local rotation of 8.8 degrees for diffusion against 0.01 for transport, and a median anisotropy of 6.30 against 3.93. The construction extends to local refinement, by transporting a city's 100 m population onto the area measure the global map assigns to it, and to a semi-discrete counterpart: 8,192 Laguerre cells of 1.00 million people each. Code, data provenance and every figure's inputs are public.
items.title: The optimal-transport cartogram: world population as a Brenier map

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22983291 . General assessment This manuscript addresses an important and underappreciated problem in computational chemistry and molecular machine learning: apparent differences in predictive performance can arise from benchmark construction and target definition rather than from intrinsic superiority of one modelling approach over another. The distinction between literature-reported absorption maxima and calculated vertical excitation energies is scientifically important, and the emphasis on genuinely external validation is a clear strength of the work. However, I find the central conclusion stronger than the evidence presently described appears to support. The results convincingly show that model performance changes substantially across datasets and label conventions. They do not yet demonstrate that label definition, rather than model capability, is the principal cause of the apparent machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. Several factors change simultaneously across the comparisons presented in the manuscript, including chemical domain, dataset provenance, transition assignment, computational protocol, sample size, and the nature of the machine-learning representation. These factors make it difficult to isolate label definition as the causal explanation. The manuscript raises a valuable methodological concern, but the title and several conclusions should either be moderated or supported by additional controlled analyses. Major comments 1. The title makes a stronger causal claim than the study design appears to establish The title states that benchmark label definition, "not model capability," explains the machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. This is a strong exclusionary claim. The results show that the apparent ranking between a Gaussian-process model and quantum-chemical calculations changes between evaluation datasets. However, label definition is not the only property that changes between these datasets. Their chemical composition, source literature, distribution of chromophores, spectral range, experimental conditions, and possibly computational protocols also differ. Therefore, demonstrating that a GP performs differently on a dataset with transition-specific labels does not by itself establish that label definition is the cause of the difference. A substantially stronger test would use the same set of molecules with two alternative target definitions—for example, a literature-reported overall λmax and an independently assigned transition-specific λmax—and evaluate both methods against both labels. A paired analysis of this type would isolate label definition while holding molecular distribution constant. Unless such a controlled analysis is provided, I suggest moderating the central conclusion to state that label definition and dataset provenance are important contributors to the reported ML advantage rather than demonstrating that they fully explain it. 2. One Gaussian-process model cannot represent "machine-learning capability" generally The machine-learning side of the comparison is represented by a Gaussian process using 256-bit Morgan fingerprints. This is a relatively specific and comparatively simple model representation. The conclusions therefore apply directly to this GP/fingerprint model, but not necessarily to molecular machine learning more broadly. Modern λmax prediction methods may use larger fingerprints, graph neural networks, message-passing architectures, pretrained molecular representations, three-dimensional information, explicit solvent descriptors, or quantum-chemical features. Such models may respond differently to both chemical and label distribution shifts. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. items.summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-

Two scoring codes are released. scorer_fixed.py is the frozen code used for the earlier evaluation of this corpus. 21_scorer_aligned.py corrects three defects found in it: temperatures reported in kelvin were compared without conversion, chemical names were compared without alias resolution, and the numeric parser took digits from chemical formulae. The third defect applies to the gold annotations as well as to the predictions. Every score in the accompanying manuscript is reported under both codes. Version 2.7 adds the scripts written after data release 2.6: manuscript edits following an external desk review (283), the supervised conditional-random-field baseline and its re-scoring on the headline path (237, 238, 254, 285; micro-F1 25.0%), the kit for a stratified random re-annotation of 250 screened articles (287), a logged re-run that records every HTTP attempt and raw response (289), and the bundle script (290). Version 2.6 adds the search scripts of rounds 1–3 to 01_corpus/ (the originals carried an API key, so the deposited copies read SCOPUS_API_KEY from the environment and are otherwise unchanged) and, in 10_analysis_v7/, the scripts that produced the manuscript and Supplementary Information edits of 27 September 2026 as auditable diffs: 265, 267, 270, 271 (identification counts from the search ledgers), 273, 275 and 277, with the bundling scripts 266 and 278. Version 2.5 adds 10_analysis_v7/265_value_normalise.py, which converts each numeric value of the released table to the unit in its unit column and writes the value_normalised and normalisation columns of data release v2.5; run without arguments, it prints every cell it could not convert. Version 2.4 adds the scripts that extend the double annotation from 25 articles to the whole 83-article test set and compute what the manuscript reports from it, all in 10_analysis_v7/ with their original names. 209_agreement_artifact_83.py builds the released comparison table over both annotation rounds and keeps only the articles in the evaluation split manifest. 204, 206 and 207 compute the agreement counts on the three bases the text distinguishes: all filled cells, the eight scored fields, and cells filled by one annotator only. 205_score_against_annotator2.py re-scores the released predictions against the second annotation instead of the first. 208_manuscript_v30_double_annotation.py applies the resulting manuscript and Supplementary Information edits of 22 September 2026 as an auditable diff. 98_annotation_artifacts.py, which builds one round's comparison sheet and which 209 imports, was missing from earlier deposits and is included here. Version 2.3 adds the scripts written after version 2.2 that produce numbers or figures in the current manuscript, all in 10_analysis_v7/ with their original names. 190_material_and_subset.py scores the material field, which the eight benchmark fields omit, and crosses the two flags released with every value (agreement between two models, and a recovered provenance span) to isolate the part of the table that needs least checking. 191_atomiclimits_overlap.py measures the overlap with the community-curated ALD Database and the field agreement on the shared articles. 186_figure6a_coreactant.py and 187_deck_v23_figures.py produce the corrected figures: 'Co-reactant' in Figure 6(a), a temperature axis truncated at 400 degrees C in Figure 7, and Figure 5 without its single-bar panel. 195_source_data_v23.py renames the Source Data sheets to the new Figure 5 panel letters. 183, 184, 188, 192, 196 and 202

items.summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-

items.summary: Replication package for the manuscript What AI Coding Agents Claim and What We Can Measure: Non-Functional Requirement Claims, Extraction Validity, and Intent–Outcome Consistency in Agent-Authored Pull Requests , prepared for submission to Empirical Software Engineering (special issue: Agentic Software Engineering). Contents: the IntentValidator pipeline source snapshot and run configurations; the per-claim datasets of the canonical agent run, of the all-repository human comparison cohort (with its protocol, draw listings and order of events) and of the superseded first human cohort, plus the re-runs that document the effect of the pipeline's timeouts; the 186-pattern NFR claim catalog, boilerplate-stripping rules and the full match table; the extraction-validity ladder and regression scripts; the manual-validation kit (stratified samples, rubric, blind labelling tool, both human raters' sheets with untouched exports and SHA-256 sums, three disclosed LLM annotation passes with per-item rationales and provenance, the LLM-judge sensitivity, the adjudication queue, a recall probe of unflagged pull requests with blind sheets and a disclosed LLM screen, and a kit for a rater from outside the author team); the consistency analysis on the human-validated claims, the Maintainability-Index floor sensitivity and the all-language cross-check of the index against independent Halstead implementations (per-claim results); every analysis script that regenerates the manuscript's numbers and figures; and a checksum manifest of every file with named reproduction checks. The archive carries the replication tree only; the manuscript itself is not included. The AIDev dataset itself is not redistributed; obtain it from its own Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.16919272). The 25 September 2026 audit revision adds explicit sampling and interpretation limitations, corrected stratification of diagnostic agreement intervals, clarified nominal instrument coverage, and reproducibility notes. Original human labels and canonical claim verdicts are preserved; catalogue label/rubric conflicts remain for human reassessment. See replication/09-paper/emse-2026/replication/REVIEW-NOTES-2026-09-25.md.

items.summary: Reproducibility archive for the article “Time-Uniform Break-Even Bounds for Label-Preserving Stopping Policies” by Burak Oktenli. The archive contains the source code, frozen model inputs, exact finite-support laws with rationally computed break-even values, the local protocol lock and its documented correction, seeds, all numerical outputs (49 CSV and 21 NPZ result files), the three result figures, the test suite and the verification scripts. All new observations are synthetic; no human-participant or personal data are included. Contents: - src/: fixed-mixture betting tests, regularized aGRAPA, Online Newton Step and checkpoint-corrected empirical Bernstein comparators; exact-truth validation; the fresh learned-policy benchmark; summaries and figures. - tests/test_r10.py: 32 executable checks. - docs/PROTOCOL.json and provenance/: protocol, seed allocation, chronology and clean-reconstruction records. - literature/: verified reference records. - MANIFEST.sha256: SHA-256 checksums for every other file in the archive. Quick check (Python 3.13 with the pinned packages in requirements.txt): python verify_release.py, then python tests/test_r10.py. Full reconstruction: python reproduce_all.py --outdir NEW_EMPTY_DIR, then python compare_reproduction.py NEW_EMPTY_DIR. This work was carried out independently by the author. It was not conducted within, funded by, or supervised by any program at Georgetown University, and the University bears no responsibility for its content.

items.summary: This record provides reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI”. The study evaluates scientific-AI fidelity by distinguishing assigned scientific objects, realized scientific objects, lineage or pathway fidelity, terminal scientific fidelity and claim boundaries.   The archive contains detailed evidence registries, comparison specifications, provenance and audit records, structured source records, manuscript source materials, display assets, and code for assembling and rendering the supplied publication materials. It also preserves the available historical CoralTemp/Coral Reef Watch daily-classification source excerpt used in the documented evidence chain.   The released materials support inspection of the reported evidence, scientific-object assignments, realized-use verification, lineage-resolved comparisons and presentation-level reproduction. They do not constitute a complete executable end-to-end reproduction of all scientific analyses. Complete raw-input and terminal-reference payloads, full benchmark execution and scoring pipelines, original scientific figure-generation programs and the original pinned scientific execution environments are not included. Public upstream scientific products and their provenance are documented in the manuscript and archive.   The archive should therefore be interpreted as a provenance-rich reproducibility and audit package rather than as a general benchmark of scientific-AI accuracy or reliability.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for "Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI"

items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. Author-created scientific text and derived materials are released under CC BY 4.0 where applicable; original author-created software is released under the MIT License unless stated otherwise.
items.title: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe from multiscale full-sky CMB reconstruction and forward generation of the reconstructed topology by a primordial magnetic source

items.summary: This record contains the public reproducibility package supporting the study “Persistent spatial organization and period-dependent associations in Beijing’s surface thermal–moisture environment”. The package includes the model-ready analytical dataset, temporal-screening and provenance records, cross-validation folds, model parameters and random-seed records, formal scripts for pooled and period-specific XGBoost–SHAP analyses, GeoDetector analysis, stored model outputs, quality-control and checksum records, and selected figure-source materials. The study comprises seven quality-controlled summer observation periods: 2000, 2004, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2016, and 2019. The primary reproducibility target of this package is the reported statistical analysis beginning from the archived ModelReady dataset. Production scripts preserve the original execution paths used during the formal analysis; users reproducing the analyses should update input and output paths to their local repository location. Upstream geospatial preprocessing scripts are retained for methodological provenance and may require the original third-party source products and local GIS configuration. Original Landsat, GLC_FCS30D, WorldPop, and Copernicus DEM source archives are not redistributed in this record and should be obtained from their respective providers. Detailed package structure, provenance, execution scope, and reproducibility notes are provided in the included README. Licensing: Data, documentation, and other original research materials created by the authors are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license. Source code created by the authors is released under the MIT License. Third-party and derived source materials remain subject to the terms of their original providers and are not relicensed by this record.
items.title: Data, code, and reproducibility materials for "Persistent spatial organization and period-dependent associations in Beijing's surface thermal–moisture environment"

items.summary: Computational reproducibility package for the study “Uncertainty-aware medical decision support using feature-value graph-augmented rough granules.”   The archive contains the complete Python source code, public UCI benchmark data snapshots and metadata, exact repeated cross-validation split indices, preprocessing and discretization records, conventional and calibrated baseline outputs, rough-granular predictions and decision statuses, granule-support and attribute-reduction outputs, one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analyses, corrected repeated-cross-validation statistical comparisons, final manuscript tables, and risk–coverage figures.   The study evaluates the Heart Disease, Breast Cancer Wisconsin Diagnostic, and Parkinsons benchmark datasets using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 10 repetitions. The feature-value graph is constructed from the measured attributes and is not an external biomedical knowledge graph. The package is provided for methodological verification and computational reproducibility and is not intended for clinical diagnosis or treatment.
items.title: Reproducibility package for uncertainty-aware medical decision support using feature-value graph-augmented rough granules
